absent: Locking, serialization and preemption rules for shadow control preparation and nested MMU switches.
Full memory layouts of control structures, VCPU nesting state and MSR list entries beyond referenced fields.
Detailed semantics of delegated helpers for control registers, exception bitmaps, TLB handling, CR3 loading, TSC composition, segment checks and MSR emulation.
Constant host-state contents and lifetime management of autoload and autostore buffers.
Complete nested entry and exit sequencing including failure reflection, migration restore and system-management-mode forced loads.

findings.text: Shadow entry controls for running L2 start from the host value, absorb the L1-requested value except for the perf-global bit, clear both EFER mode and load bits, then opportunistically set them again when the processor offers EFER loading, using long-mode status and host-versus-guest EFER comparison to reduce later writes; authoritative EFER handling happens later.

Shadow exit controls for running L2 reuse the host value because the physical exit lands in host context while the L1 view stays emulated; the EFER load bit is set only when the processor offers it and guest and host EFER differ, otherwise cleared, with later EFER handling allowed to adjust it.

Event injection state follows a pending-entry flag: when set, the shadow copies intr info, error code, instruction length and interruptibility from L1 and marks NMI unmasked tracking as the inverse of the NMI-blocked indication; when clear, the shadow clears intr info and leaves other fields untouched in this fragment.

Effective guest EFER for nested entry prefers L1-provided guest EFER when entry is pending and L1 asked for EFER loading; otherwise long-mode request bits are forced on or off onto the current EFER while preserving remaining bits, yielding forced long mode or forced non-long mode.

Shadow uses no link pointer. When VPID support is enabled globally, it selects the L2-specific VPID only if L1 enabled VPID and such an identifier exists; otherwise it reuses the L1 identifier so disabled cases share host identifier zero and retain translations for other identifiers instead of flushing excessively.

One-time shadow initialization runs once per VCPU, guarded by a flag. It fixes MSR store and load addresses to host-owned buffers while leaving counts variable, programs virtualization-exception address when present, points at the shadow MSR bitmap, disables all VM functions and page-modification logging with empty index, blocks ENCLS exits, sets a dedicated nested posted-interrupt vector, and applies notify window when enabled, before establishing constant host state.

A per-entry preparation routine consumes L1 control state and a flag indicating whether the call comes from emulated entry, refreshes shadow control and guest state for L2, and reports success or invalid-entry with a default failure code for the caller to reflect to L1.

Flags for L2 always come from L1 control state. Debug registers, CET state, bound configuration and PAT follow load-request gating: L1 values are adopted only on pending entry with the corresponding load bit, otherwise pre-entry saved values or current architectural values return, with debug control narrowed to supported bits and PAT additionally gated by host entry configuration.

Trap configuration merges L1 and host desires by updating the exception bitmap and narrowing host-owned CR0 bits with the L1 mask before publishing the inverted mask. Nested TSC offset and scaling are composed from L1 and L2 components and published to the shadow, with multiplier published only when scaling support exists.
L2 TSC offset is taken from L1 only when L1 enabled TSC offsetting, otherwise zero; L2 multiplier is taken from L1 only when both offsetting and scaling are enabled, otherwise a capability default.

L2 preparation includes a TLB transition flush, a switch to nested EPT mode when L1 enabled EPT, installation of effective CR0 and CR4 with mask-aware read shadows overwritten afterwards, and derivation plus installation of effective EFER which may further adjust entry and exit controls and EFER images.
Visible CR0 and CR4 values combine L1 guest value and read shadow through the guest-host mask, taking guest bits where host does not intercept and shadow bits where it does.

Nested EPT activation asserts the VCPU is not already in nested paging, points address translation at the guest MMU, refreshes the shadow EPTP, and installs handlers for fetching the L1 EPT pointer, reading PD pointers, and injecting EPT faults.
Shadow EPT construction derives execute-only permission and large-page level from L1-exposed EPT capabilities together with access-dirty support, mode-based execution support and the L1 EPT pointer.

Infrequent guest-state synchronization includes CET state gated by its load request, extended-state exit bitmap gated by XSAVES exposure, EOI bitmaps gated by APIC virtualization, plus segment selectors, limits, rights and bases with descriptor-table bases refreshed only when the second enlightened guest group is dirty and system-enter state with pending debug refreshed only when the first group is dirty, with bound config conditionally refreshed, segment cache invalidated after segment updates, and CR4 mask refreshed.

Page-fault filtering cannot always merge host and L1 desires: when the host needs its own intercepts the shadow forces an exit on every L2 fault by zeroing mask and match and relying on merged bitmap to request exits; otherwise it adopts L1 mask and match verbatim.

When L1 asked to store TSC on exit, the shadow temporarily appends TSC to its own store list and publishes an incremented count while keeping the persistent software count unchanged and recording the slot; otherwise it publishes the unchanged count and marks the slot absent, with overflow guarded.
Presence check for an MSR in the L1 exit-store list walks the guest list in order, returning false immediately on any unreadable entry and true on first index match, otherwise false.

Guest state acceptance is permissive under unrestricted execution and otherwise checks segment validity differently for real and protected modes, covering real-mode segments or privilege, code, stack, data, task and descriptor-table segments, with instruction pointer and flags checks noted as future work.

Stack and instruction pointers come from L1 and enlightened cleanliness is marked fully clean to compensate for hosts that never clear it. CR3 loading is delegated with EPT awareness and may veto entry; on EPT the shadow guest CR3 is written eagerly so exits without running still propagate it, as with halt-state interception. Page-table pointers for PAE under EPT refresh late after EFER and control registers settle, and perf-global requests are emulated through an MSR write when supported.

Entry preparation can fail entry with a default code when forced from emulated entry with invalid guest state under restricted execution, when CR3 loading rejects the L1 value, or when perf-global emulation reports an error; these paths return invalid without running L2.

Feature predicates are single-bit tests: posted-interrupt support is the posted bit in pin-based controls, XSAVES exposure is the XSAVES secondary execution bit, and mode-based EPT execution is its secondary execution bit.
The EPT table to shadow is the EPT pointer field of L1 control state, and access-dirty enablement is the AD bit within that pointer value.
L2 TSC offset and multiplier accessors are file-external helpers that let other units obtain L1-programmed timing adjustments for nested execution.
Detailed guest-state validation is file-external so callers outside its defining file can reuse the segment checks, while the header wrapper adds an unrestricted-execution shortcut.
